features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The level of formal academic training or degree attainment the applicant claims as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is stated, or the educational background is unclear.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation in a relevant technical field.
States a master's degree in a relevant technical field.
States a doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing agent-based systems with explicit control boundaries, supervision, permissions, or supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as evidenced through concrete engineering examples or system improvements.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic strength is given.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example.
The letter gives one clear example of algorithmic or data-structure improvement.
The letter gives multiple or especially strong examples tied to meaningful system simplification, performance, or correctness gains.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: The extent of real production experience with AI or LLM systems, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Whether the applicant frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through good defaults, low-friction tooling, and attention to internal users.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How concretely the letter substantiates claims with specific examples, named systems, technical mechanisms, or other grounded evidence.

levels.descriptor: Mostly relies on self-assertion, with little concrete support for claims.
Includes some specifics, but few mechanics, numbers, or outcomes.
Provides several concrete examples with technical detail, counts, or before-and-after effects.
Repeatedly grounds claims in vivid, trust-building evidence, including technical mechanics and clear impact.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central, substantial, and production-relevant Go appears in the applicant's experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Whether the letter explains the outcomes, effects, or measurable results of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Maintainer and reliability mindset
features.description: A bias toward durable, maintainable, rigorously engineered systems with attention to failure modes, testing, and long-term operability.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.name: Narrative cohesion and distinctiveness
features.description: How coherent, memorable, and well-shaped the letter's story, flow, or voice is beyond a checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-minded or adversarial security practice outside normal product work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for code used beyond the applicant's employer, from upstream fixes to sustained public maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Overall production engineering experience
features.description: The overall depth of relevant production-software experience when a dimension explicitly combines professional tenure with substantial shipping and operational responsibility.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives thin or barely qualifying evidence of production software experience.
The letter shows solid early-career production experience with at least some testing, maintenance, or launch responsibility.
The letter shows multiple years of work and several production systems launched or maintained.
The letter shows extensive experience well beyond the minimums, with repeated launches and sustained ownership of production systems.

features.name: Ownership level
features.description: The degree of autonomy, seniority, and direct responsibility the applicant claims for the systems or work they describe.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, rigor, or systems depth of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation for foundational or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production service scope
features.description: The breadth or depth of hands-on ownership the applicant claims across launching, maintaining, testing, or operating production services.

levels.descriptor: Little production breadth is evidenced, or shipped systems are not clearly described.
The letter points to work on 1 to 2 production services.
The letter points to work on 3 to 4 production services.
The letter points to work on 5 or more production services.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How concretely and seriously Python is shown as a real working language for production systems, tooling, automation, or services.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: The amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant presents, mainly in duration or seniority terms.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of clearly relevant experience, or tenure is not stated.
About 2 to 3 years of relevant experience; clears the minimum but is still early-career for this role.
About 4 to 5 years of relevant experience; solid mid-level tenure.
6 or more years of relevant experience; deep tenure for this opening.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically the letter explains and maps the applicant's motivation and background to this exact role, team, or posting.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses through review, threat modeling, validation, or remediation follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How clearly the letter understands the role as scaling scarce security expertise through automation for response, triage, analysis, and secure workflows.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The strength of formal third-party security credentials or certifications cited as evidence of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
A baseline credential is mentioned, such as Security+, indicating foundational security study.
A stronger hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive testing ability.

features.name: Security engineering mindset
features.description: The seriousness and thoughtfulness of the applicant's philosophy, identity, or motivation around security as an engineering discipline.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The surface-level professionalism of the letter's prose, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy-editing accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Heterogeneous dimensions that do not clearly fit a larger recurring construct here, such as language breadth or collaboration style with specialist partners.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.
